subject: DI03000081

body.en:
Definition

Astatic device transfers ACpower between circuits through mutual flux at the same frequency.

Classification / representative type

  • Core type:windings surround two principal limbs;shell type:core surrounds the central winding stack.Oil-filled/dry-type classification concerns insulation/cooling,not the same geometric distinction.
  • Step-up/down describes terminal voltage relation,not a new operating principle.Two-winding units can provide galvanic separation;autotransformers do not.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Laminated grain-oriented electrical-steel core provides a low-reluctance path;thin insulated sheets suppress eddy currents.Magnetic joints are designed to limit reluctance/noise.
  2. Primary and secondary windings use insulated copper or aluminium sized for current,loss and thermal limits.They are not electrically joined in an ordinary two-winding transformer.
  3. LVwinding is generally nearer the core and HVoutside it to reduce required insulation to the earthed core,subject to actual design.
  4. Paper,pressboard,varnish/enamel and approved solid/liquid insulation separate turns,layers,windings and earth;clearances are rated design features.
  5. Core-type coils are divided between limbs in suitable concentric arrangements to reduce leakage and improve magnetic coupling.
  6. Tank,oil/radiators or dry-type air passages remove heat;oil also insulates in an oil-filled unit.Small dry teaching transformers may have none of the large oil accessories.
  7. Bushings/terminal boards provide insulated connections;clamps,earthing points and nameplate identify mechanical security,protection and ratings.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. An ACprimary voltage drives an exciting current and establishes alternating core flux.
  2. Common flux links both windings and induces EMFaccording to the number of turns.
  3. With secondary open,the primary draws a small no-load current containing magnetising and core-loss components.
  4. Connecting a load causes secondary current whose MMFopposes the original flux change under Lenz law.
  5. The primary automatically draws additional load-component current to balance secondary ampere-turns,keeping flux approximately fixed by V/f.
  6. Winding resistance/leakage cause voltage drops and copper loss;core loss and excitation remain present even at no external load.
  7. Input power therefore equals useful output plus losses;frequency is unchanged and steady DCoperation is not allowed.

Applications

Power supplies,distribution,isolation where certified,and impedance matching within ratings.

Limitations and safety

Astep-down voltage is not proof of safe isolation.Insulation class,earthing,protection and thermal limits govern actual use.

Why kVA?

Heating depends chiefly on V/fand current;load pfis external to the transformer.

Understand the idea

The central limb carries the common winding assembly;the return flux divides between two outer limbs.

Explanation and application

  • At symmetrical design each outer limb carries about half the central-limb flux;central-limb cross-section is correspondingly selected for the same allowable flux density.
  • Sandwich/interleaved HV/LVcoil sections are commonly used to reduce leakage and obtain mechanical support,with insulation maintained between sections.
  • Core-type concentric versus shell-type sandwich is a useful textbook comparison,not an absolute rule for every specialised design.
  • Both follow mutual induction and the same EMFequation.Selection depends on insulation,cooling,leakage,manufacturing and mechanical requirements.

Understand the idea

Assume sinusoidal common flux Φ=Φm sinωtand RMSwinding EMF.

Explanation and application

  • Instantaneous emf magnitude follows Nturn dΦ/dt;peak=2πfNΦm.RMS=peak/√2=4.44fNΦmapproximately.
  • E1/E2=N1/N2=a.For an ideal transformer,V1/V2=aand I1/I2=1/a;real terminal ratios differ slightly under load due to drops.
  • State whether a=N1/N2or k=N2/N1is used;both conventions exist.The symbol alone is not a definition.
  • At given turns,flux is approximately proportional to V/f.Low frequency at unchanged voltage risks overflux/saturation and overheating.
  • EMFequation gives induced RMSemf,not exact loaded secondary terminal voltage;include winding drops when required.

Given and assumptions

50Hz,N1=500turns,Φm0.002Wb,N2=100turns;use the textbook4.44factor.

Step-by-step solution

  1. E1=4.44×50×500×0.002=222V;E2=44.4V;a=5.
  2. For ideal500VAat these voltages,I1=2.25225A,I2=11.2613A.Current ratio is inverse of voltage ratio.

Interpretation and check

4.44is rounded fromπ√2;do not claim greater physical accuracy than the input data.

Understand the idea

Voltage governs flux/core loss and current governs copper heating;load power factor is not set by the transformer.

Explanation and application

  • Single-phase Srated=VratedIrated;actual useful output P=VIcosφfor a sinusoidal load.At1kVAand pf0.8,the output is800W,not1kW.
  • Nameplate includes frequency,voltages,kVA,currents,connections/cooling and insulation/temperature information.Select actual design limits,not only the turns ratio.
  • Adual-voltage or tapped winding needs the manufacturer series/parallel link diagram;wrong links can short sections or overvolt insulation.

Understand the idea

Take V1as the horizontal RMSreference and neglect the small series drop for the basic diagram.

Explanation and application

  • I0=Ic−jIm:Icin phase with V1supplies core loss;Imlags V1by90°and magnetises the core.I0lags by an angle less than90°.
  • With sinusoidal approximate magnetisation,flux is in phase with Imand lags V1by90°.Real I0may be distorted by saturation.
  • Dot/terminal references determine EMFarrow signs;never mix a counter-emf loop reference with a positive-at-dot terminal-voltage reference without reversing the arrow.
  • No-load input is not zero:core loss predominates,but small winding copper loss and instrument losses may exist.

Understand the idea

Refer quantities to one side and choose V2as reference for an approximate loaded diagram.

Explanation and application

  • Additional primary ampere-turns balance secondary load ampere-turns;I1is the vector sum of referred load current and I0,not their scalar sum.
  • Leakage flux links only its own winding effectively;its induced drop is represented by jIX.With common reference side,E≈V2+I2(Req+jXeq).
  • Lagging current gives positive resistive/reactive contributions to usual regulation;leading current can reduce or reverse regulation.
  • Leakage reactance is not winding DCresistance;both affect voltage drop,but only resistive loss directly appears as I²Rheat.

Understand the idea

Let a=N1/N2;refer the secondary to primary before combining impedances.

Explanation and application

  • V2′=aV2,I2′=I2/a,Z2′=a²Z2;thus R2′=a²R2and X2′=a²X2.Power is invariant under ideal referral.
  • Primary-referred Req=R1+a²R2,Xeq=X1+a²X2.The exact circuit retains an ideal transformer and the shunt branch in its actual position.
  • Rcmodels core-loss power;Xmmodels magnetising reactive demand.They are parallel,not series,branches in the usual exciting circuit.
  • In the approximate circuit,the exciting branch is moved to input and small I0-related series drops are neglected;state this approximation before calculation.

Given and assumptions

a2,R1=1Ω,X1=2Ω,R2=0.25Ω,X2=0.5Ω.

Step-by-step solution

  1. Primary:Req=1+4×0.25=2Ω;Xeq=2+4×0.5=4Ω.
  2. Secondary:Req=1/4+0.25=0.5Ω;Xeq=2/4+0.5=1Ω.
  3. At I1=2A,I2=4A,both references predict copper loss8W.Do not add1Ωand0.25Ωwithout referral.

Interpretation and check

The a²factor changes ohms,not physical losses.

Understand the idea

Aload test measures actual input/output at declared load,pfand thermal conditions.

Explanation and application

  • Regulation%=(VNL−VFL)/VFL×100at the stated primary V/fand load condition;state the chosen definition because some specifications use other bases.
  • Approximate regulation fraction≈I2(Reqcosφ+Xeqsinφ)/V2for lagging load;for leading load use−Xeqsin|φ|instead.All quantities must share the same reference side.
  • η=Pout/Pin=Pout/(Pout+Pcore+Pcu+other losses).At fraction xof rated current,Pcu≈x²PcuFLat unchanged resistance.
  • At fixed voltage/frequency,pfand resistance,the simple model gives maximum ηwhen x²PcuFL=Pcore.This is not automatically full load.
  • Direct loading dissipates real output power in the load bank;observe current/temperature/voltage ratings and qualified supervision.

Understand the idea

Apply rated voltage/frequency only to the approved chosen winding;leave the other winding open and guarded.

Explanation and application

  • Measure V0,I0,W0on the energised side.W0≈core loss only when small no-load copper/instrument losses are negligible.
  • cosφ0=W0/(V0I0);Ic=W0/V0;Im=√(I0²−Ic²);Rc=V0/Ic;Xm=V0/Im.
  • Parameters belong to the energised reference side.Check0≤W0≤V0I0;a negative radicand or pfabove1means data/setup/range/model must be investigated.
  • The open winding is not dead:induced voltage may be much higher than applied voltage.Follow approved test links and instrument ratings.

Understand the idea

The shorted winding must be prepared only while dead;apply a LOWcontrolled voltage to the other winding until rated current,not rated voltage,is reached.

Explanation and application

  • Measure Vsc,Isc,Wsc;Zeq=Vsc/Isc,Req=Wsc/Isc²,Xeq=√(Zeq²−Req²)on the measurement side.
  • At reduced V,the core flux/loss is small,so Wsc≈copper loss at the measured current.At rated current it approximates full-load copper loss at test temperature.
  • If Iscis not rated current,rescale copper loss by(Irated/Isc)²where the resistance-temperature model permits.Do not label any Wscas full-load loss.
  • Use rated current limiting,approved shorting links and immediate stop criteria;applying full rated voltage across an SCtest is dangerous.

Given and assumptions

1kVA,200/100V;OCon100Vside:V0=100V,I0=0.5A,W0=30W;SCon200Vside:Vsc10V,Isc5A,Wsc25W.

Step-by-step solution

  1. OC:pf0=0.6,Ic0.3A,Im0.4A,Rc333.333Ω,Xm250Ωon100Vside.
  2. SC:Zeq2Ω,Req1Ω,Xeq√3=1.73205Ωon200Vside;divide by4to obtain0.5Ω,0.25Ω,0.433013Ωon100Vside.
  3. At full load pf0.8lagging,Pout800W;η=800/(800+30+25)=93.5673%.Approx regulation=(10×(0.25×0.8+0.433013×0.6))/100=4.59808%.
  4. At pf0.8leading,approx regulation=−0.598076%.At half load,pf0.8,Pout400W and copper loss6.25W;η=91.6905%.

Interpretation and check

All values are calculated expected results.The exact circuit and hot resistance can change actual results.

Understand the idea

Distribution transformers remain energised even when lightly loaded;use a complete daily energy schedule.

Explanation and application

  • ηall-day=Σ(Pout,k tk)/[Σ(Pout,k tk)+Pcoretenergised+Σ(xk²PcuFLtk)]in the simple loss model.
  • Use kWand hours consistently for kWh.Core loss accrues for the actual energised duration,not automatically only the loaded hours.
  • Do not average several instantaneous efficiency percentages;their energy weights differ.Daily loading/pfand constant versus variable losses determine the result.

Given and assumptions

10kVAunit,core loss100W,full-load copper loss200W;8hours full load pf0.8,8hours half load pf0.8,8hours no load;energised24hours.

Step-by-step solution

  1. Output energy=8kW×8h+4kW×8h=96kWh.
  2. Core energy=0.1×24=2.4kWh;copper energy=0.2×8+0.05×8=2kWh.
  3. Input energy100.4kWh;ηall-day=96/100.4=95.6175%.

Interpretation and check

The no-load interval still incurs core loss because the unit remains energised.

Understand the idea

These tests require verified dead links and qualified supervision;wrong polarity can create damaging current.

Explanation and application

  • Polarity test:use an approved low-ACseries comparison.If the free-end voltage is the sum,the chosen connection is series-aiding;if the difference,series-opposing.Mark corresponding instantaneous-polarity dots from the known test connection.
  • Parallel operation needs equal voltage ratio/taps,correct polarity,matching frequency and compatible impedance magnitude/angle;three-phase operation additionally needs matching phase sequence/displacement.
  • With equal no-load voltages and compatible impedances,I1/I2=Z2/Z1as a complex relation,kVAsharing follows rated percentage impedances.Use each unit current limit,not just total bank rating.
  • Sumpner/back-to-back test uses two suitable identical transformers:primaries parallel at rated V/f,secondaries in verified series opposition,and a separate controlled low-voltage injection to circulate rated current.
  • Main input approximately supplies total core loss;auxiliary injection approximately supplies total copper loss at the circulating current.Split losses per unit only when the identical-unit assumption holds.
  • It permits heating/full-load-loss assessment without dissipating full rated output in an external load.Not a DIYseries connection;verify zero resultant secondary voltage before approved injection.

Definition

One continuous tapped winding acts as both input and output;there is no galvanic separation.

Classification / representative type

  • Fixed-tap and variable-slider types;step-up/down depends on the applied and taken terminals.Avariac is a variable autotransformer,not an isolation transformer.

Construction — part and purpose

  1. Laminated magnetic core supports alternating flux with low core loss.
  2. Continuous insulated winding is divided functionally into series and common portions by a tap.
  3. Common section connects electrically to both source and load;its conductor current is a phasor difference in the ideal step-down case.
  4. Series section carries the appropriate line-side current and supports only the difference voltage.
  5. Tap/slider assembly must have specified current/contact ratings and protection;ordinary taps are changed dead unless designed for on-load change.
  6. Insulation,enclosure,earthing and terminals must be rated for the highest voltage to earth,not only the nominal low output.

Working — sequence and reason

  1. Apply rated-frequency ACto the specified input turns;alternating core flux develops.
  2. Each turn has approximately equal induced volts per turn,so the chosen turn ratio sets output voltage.
  3. Load current flows through the tap and common connection;some output power passes conductively from source.
  4. The remainder is transferred by induction between series/common winding portions.
  5. For ideal step-down k=VL/VH,IH=kILand the common-winding current magnitude is IL−IHfor a common pf.
  6. Inductively transformed kVA=(1−k)Sthrough;material saving is greatest when ratios are close to1,but short-circuit impedance/protection become important.
  7. An open common winding or wrong connection can expose the load to dangerous voltage;never treat an adjusted low output as isolated safe power.

Applications

Voltage adjustment and compatible-system interconnection where isolation is not required.

Limitations and safety

No isolation and potentially high fault current;approved rated trainers and supervision only.
